name: Sonnet price momentum
strategy: Rotate into laggard defensive/value sectors (healthcare, financials, duration) while shorting exhausted momentum extremes (gold miners, gold, leveraged semis) — a mean-reversion/relative-value book, not trend-following.

positions.thesis: $157.41 vs 52-wk high $165.71 (95% of range); best-confirmed laggard catch-up trade in the book. Unchanged, highest conviction leg.
Healthcare rotation confirmed near 52-wk highs; kept at half Round 2's size specifically to hold cross-book overlap well under the 50% limit.
Financials strength confirmed near 52-wk highs; kept at roughly two-thirds Round 2's size specifically to hold cross-book overlap well under the 50% limit.
$77.93 vs 52-wk high $78.35; regional banks confirming the financials rotation with no Round 2 overlap. Unchanged.

Duration carry thesis is weakening in real time -- down from ~$84 to $82.04 over three weeks as yields rise on oil-driven inflation fears. Trimmed 12%->8% and tightened the stop to -6% to limit downside rather than removing the mandate's third pillar entirely.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: XBI/XLV/XLF/KRE all confirmed near their 52-week highs and are left unchanged. TLT's duration thesis is weakening -- it fell from ~$84 (7/28) to $82.04 (8/14) as yields rose on oil-driven inflation fears -- so trimmed 12%->8% and tightened the stop -8%->-6% to cap further downside while keeping token defensive-duration exposure per mandate. GLD short is closed: gold has rallied ~9% off its 7/20 low ($367.60->$401.48), the same squeeze signature already seen in GDX (which stopped this exact book out on 8/7) and now separately flagged in the Round 2 TQQQ short too -- three shorts squeezing simultaneously across two complexes is systemic evidence this isn't 'exhausted momentum,' it's a live squeeze. Closing rather than repeating a trade type that has already failed twice for this manager, freeing capital to cash.
novelty: Post-rebalance this book is 73% long / 27% cash with the GLD short fully closed, so it now shares only two symbols with the Round 2 book (XLV, XLF) held at roughly half Round 2's weight; overlap works out to about 20 points of same-direction gross against this book's 73% gross (~27%), well under the 50% cap, while XBI, KRE and TLT (53 of the 73 long points) carry zero Round 2 exposure and express the mean-reversion/laggard-catch-up mandate on names Round 2 does not touch.
research_notes:
Read the account packet first (NAV, P&L, standing-order fires). Web search budget was exhausted for the session before I could run any WebSearch queries, so all market research came from WebFetch against stockanalysis.com (current quote + 52-week range pages, and history/ pages for daily closes) for every held or watched symbol: XLF, XLV, XLE, IWM, TQQQ, XBI, KRE, TLT, GLD, SOXL, GDX.

Key findings as of 2026-08-14 close:
- XLF, XLV, XLE, XBI, KRE all trading within ~1-5% of their 52-week highs -- every long-momentum leg in both books is confirmed and working.
- IWM closed at $305.09 vs a 52-wk high of $305.18 -- essentially an all-time high, the single strongest confirmation in either book.
- TQQQ (Round 2's short) rallied ~33% off its 7/29 low ($57.75) to $76.79 by 8/14, now at 87% of its 52-week range -- pulled up daily closes and confirmed this is a live, ongoing squeeze, not noise, matching the exact pattern (SOXL 8/4, GDX 8/7) that already stopped this manager out twice per the packet's own history.
- GLD (Round 3's short) rallied ~9% off its 7/20 low ($367.60) to $401.48 by 8/14; GDX (the leveraged cousin already stopped out on 8/7) is also up strongly (+56% trailing year, near highs) -- gold is not exhausted, it's continuing the same squeeze that already burned this book once in this complex.
- TLT (Round 3) fell from ~$84 (7/28) to $82.04 (8/14) as Treasury yields rose on oil-price-driven inflation concerns -- the "rate-cut duration carry" thesis is not confirming in price, unlike every other long in the book.

Net decision: kept every confirmed long-momentum position unchanged (or sized up where confirmation strengthened, IWM), closed both shorts that are now showing the identical squeeze signature that has already cost this manager two stop-outs this cycle (TQQQ in Round 2, GLD in Round 3) rather than waiting for a third stop to confirm it, and trimmed/tightened the one long whose price action is contradicting its thesis (TLT). Verified the resulting Round 3 book keeps same-direction overlap with the new Round 2 book to about 27% of gross, comfortably under the 50% cap.
